main_risk: Consensus of several annotators is itself an estimate, and systematic annotator biases shared across annotators would not be exposed by consensus comparison.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Ground-truth boxes are treated as strictly more accurate than model outputs, making all deviation model error.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Averaging over thousands of noisy examples during training lets the model estimate the annotation distribution's center, which beats any individual sample from that distribution.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Triple-annotate a hundred objects, compare one detector's boxes and the original labels against the consensus in one annotation-plus-analysis cycle.

one_line_idea: Model confusion matrices partially replicate annotator confusion: class-label errors in detection datasets are structured by visual similarity and annotation workflow, and models inherit these exact confusions, inflating measured semantic error.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Class labels in detection datasets contain errors that are systematic, similar-looking categories and interface-adjacent choices get swapped, and evaluation treats the annotated label as truth when scoring model classification.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The label-error confusion structure of a dataset, estimable from re-annotation samples, aligns measurably with the confusion structure of models trained on it, beyond what visual similarity alone predicts, so part of measured classification error reflects faithful learning of annotation mistakes, and cleaning training labels would reduce exactly the aligned confusions.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Confusion-matrix alignment between annotator errors and model errors will exceed the alignment predicted by an independent visual-similarity model, and label-cleaning interventions on training data will reduce the aligned confusion cells disproportionately on cleanly re-annotated test data.
why_important: Distinguishing inherited-label error from perceptual error changes both the interpretation of benchmark semantic-error rates and the expected return of label-cleaning versus model-improvement investments.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Label noise inheritance is studied for classification datasets, and the annotator-model confusion-alignment methodology for detection labels may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Estimate annotation confusion from expert re-annotation samples, estimate model confusions on cleaned test data, fit alignment beyond visual-similarity controls, and run a training-label-cleaning intervention arm.
main_risk: Expert re-annotation defines the reference truth, and expert disagreement on genuinely ambiguous categories limits how sharply annotator error can be estimated.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Model classification errors on benchmarks are read as pure perception failures against a clean reference.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Models are optimized to reproduce the labeling process, not the world, and any systematic component of the labeling process is signal to the optimizer, indistinguishable from truth.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Re-annotate the most confused category pairs for one dataset sample and check whether annotation swaps concentrate on the same pairs as model confusions.

one_line_idea: Sparse-annotation training teaches contextual self-censorship: detectors trained under incomplete labeling learn context-dependent suppression of valid detections, producing deployment blind spots that complete-annotation fine-tuning reverses.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Several large detection datasets label only a subset of present instances per image by protocol, and training treats unlabeled regions as negatives, penalizing the detector for finding real but unlabeled objects.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The false-negative supervision of sparse annotation is context-structured, certain categories are systematically under-labeled in certain scene types, so detectors learn scene-conditional suppression rules, detecting an object in one context and suppressing the same appearance in another, and these learned blind spots persist invisibly because evaluation shares the annotation sparsity.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On exhaustively re-annotated evaluation subsets, sparse-trained detectors will show context-dependent recall gaps aligned with the training data's under-labeling structure, and brief fine-tuning on completely annotated data will recover recall specifically in the previously suppressed contexts.
why_important: Context-conditional blind spots are the worst kind of deployment failure, systematic, silent, and correlated with scene type, and identifying their annotation-protocol origin gives a concrete remediation path.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Missing-label training effects are studied as uniform noise, and the context-structured suppression hypothesis with its persistence and reversal predictions may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Map under-labeling structure of a sparse dataset via exhaustive re-annotation samples, evaluate sparse-trained detectors on complete annotations stratified by that structure, and run the recovery fine-tuning arm.
main_risk: Exhaustive re-annotation at sufficient scale is the main cost, and under-labeling structure estimation needs enough samples per context cell.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Missing labels are treated as diluted supervision that mildly lowers recall uniformly rather than as structured anti-supervision.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The optimizer receives consistent negative gradient for specific appearance-context combinations, which is precisely a training signal for conditional suppression, not random noise.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Exhaustively annotate a small scene-stratified image sample, evaluate one sparse-trained detector, and look for context-aligned recall gaps in a short annotation sprint.

one_line_idea: Model-assisted annotation launders foundation-model blind spots into ground truth: datasets built with detector-in-the-loop labeling inherit the assistant's misses, making successor models' shared failures unmeasurable.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Modern dataset construction increasingly uses model proposals to accelerate annotation, annotators verify and correct machine suggestions rather than searching images unaided, and verification-mode annotators are known in human-factors research to under-correct omissions relative to commissions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detector-assisted annotation transfers the assistant model's recall blind spots into the dataset because annotators rarely add instances the assistant missed, so datasets carry a fingerprint of the assisting model's failure modes, successor models trained and evaluated on such data appear to solve categories they share blind spots on, and cross-generation blind-spot persistence is measurable by comparing assisted against unaided annotation of identical images.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Dual-protocol annotation of the same image set, machine-assisted versus unaided, will show the assisted protocol missing instances concentrated exactly where the assisting detector scores lowest, and models evaluated on assisted annotations will overstate recall on those strata relative to unaided-annotation evaluation.
why_important: As assisted labeling becomes universal, evaluation and training data converge toward what current models already see, structurally hiding shared failures from every future benchmark, a self-sealing contamination loop the field is not monitoring.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Automation bias in annotation is documented in human-factors work, and its quantification as a detection-dataset contamination mechanism with cross-generation consequences may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Annotate one image set under both protocols with matched annotator pools, map missing-instance strata against the assistant's confidence landscape, and quantify evaluation distortion for several successor models under each ground truth.
main_risk: Protocol comparisons need careful annotator matching and incentive design, since unaided annotation is slower and fatigue could mimic the effect under study.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Machine-assisted annotation is treated as strictly beneficial, faster with equal quality, because humans verify every machine suggestion.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Verification workflows direct human attention to what the machine found, and omissions generate no verification prompt, so the protocol structurally under-samples exactly the assistant's blind spots.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Have annotators label fifty images with and without machine proposals and compare the sets of found instances against each other in a two-day annotation exercise.
